answer: An agent market requires every identity to lock 100 tokens for 30 days before it can bid for work, and caps each identity at one active job. Whether an agent calls itself raven, canyon, or ember, the same rule applies. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up 100,000 tokens for a month. The attacker can recover the stake later, but must finance that capital and forgo other uses of it, making mass identities costly.
